content: Ritonavir increases the plasma levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction necessitates avoiding coadministration or using an alternative drug. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of riociguat by reducing its metabolism via hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. This interaction requires avoiding coadministration or selecting an alternative therapy. If used, monitor for signs of hypotension and adjust the dose as needed. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use with combined P-glycoprotein and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided due to the risk of significant increases in rivaroxaban levels and bleeding complications. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible. Ritonavir enhances the toxicity of rosuvastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID in patients with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use in patients with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per its prescribing information. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the original selumetinib dose. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients receiving indinavir with ritonavir should not exceed 25 mg of sildenafil for erectile dysfunction within a 48-hour period. Sildenafil use for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with ritonavir is not recommended. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of topical sofpironium by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of sotagliflozin by inducing glucuronidation via UGT1A9. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Sotorasib reduces the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or refer to the prescribing information for dosage adjustments. Ritonavir and sparsentan may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or interrupt sparsentan treatment if unavoidable. St. John’s Wort decreases ritonavir levels by inducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by inhibiting OATP1-mediated active secretion, potentially increasing plasma concentrations. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Stop tadalafil at least 24 hours before initiating protease inhibitors (PIs) and restart seven days after PI initiation at 20 mg once daily, increasing to 40 mg based on tolerability. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite N-desmethyl tamoxifen. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Tepotinib increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as per its product labeling. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of thioridazine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tucatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the CYP3A substrate dose as per product labeling. Ritonavir and vemurafenib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of vortioxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Reduce the vortioxetine dose by 50% when coadministered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Ritonavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the pre-inhibition dose. Ritonavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor for hyperglycemia. Ritonavir reduces the effects of albiglutide due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor for hyperglycemia. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Amobarbital decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. Aprepitant raises ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Armodafinil reduces ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir may increase or decrease artemether levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir may increase or decrease lumefantrine levels when coadministered with artemether/lumefantrine. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir decreases artesunate levels by inducing its metabolism, potentially reducing its efficacy. Monitor for decreased artesunate effectiveness. Atazanavir increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and OATP1B1 transport. Adjust the atogepant dose to 10 mg or 30 mg daily when coadministered with OATP inhibitors. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of atomoxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atorvastatin also increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin raises ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. However, ritonavir may also decrease bazedoxifene levels by inducing metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir raises the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone levels, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Adjust therapy and monitor closely.
